clue.text: Inexperienced anchors put back where headlines are made

parts.note: someone inexperienced is new to the job

indicators.note: put back tells us to read the word for anchors from right to left

parts.note: to anchor a ship is to moor it, so anchors means moors

explanation.surface: Green television presenters are returned to the office where the day's top stories are written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anchors' looks like news presenters, but here it is the verb: to anchor a ship is to moor it.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper or broadcaster's newsroom is the office where stories and their headlines are written.

clue.text: Large nest egg: your retirement is easy from the start

indicators.note: from the start tells us to take the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A financial adviser says a big nest egg makes retirement comfortable right from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nest egg' reads as savings, but 'nest' belongs to the definition and 'egg' starts the run of first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is the large nest of an eagle or other bird of prey, built high on a crag.

clue.text: POW's parasites? They build up gradually in the damp

definitions.text: They build up gradually in the damp

parts.note: a stalag was a German camp for prisoners of war, so it belongs to the POW
mites are tiny parasitic creatures

explanation.surface: A question asks whether prison-camp lice are the creatures that slowly accumulate in wet places.
explanation.walkthrough: A stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalagmites are mineral columns that grow upward slowly from the floors of wet limestone caves.

clue.text: Confederacy endures having leader demoted as far as possible

indicators.text: having leader demoted as far as possible
indicators.note: the leading letter is moved down to the very bottom of the word, as far as it can go

parts.note: to hold out is to endure or keep resisting

explanation.surface: The Southern rebels keep fighting even after their commander is sacked to the lowest rank.
explanation.walkthrough: The H at the front of HOLDSOUT goes to the end. The Old South is the American South of the Confederate states.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old South names the pre-Civil War slave states, the region that formed the Confederacy.

clue.text: It helps to read fine print as gang family signs arrangement

definitions.text: It helps to read fine print

indicators.note: arrangement means the letters of the three preceding words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone deciphers small type as a sign language used by a criminal clan.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnifying glass is a hand lens that enlarges small text so it can be read easily.

clue.text: Woolly decoration, an order presented after ceremony

indicators.note: presented after puts the order's letters behind the word for ceremony

parts.note: pomp is splendid ceremony
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A medal is handed over after a formal occasion, alongside a fluffy ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM (Order of Merit) is a British honour in the monarch's gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompom is a small fluffy ball of wool used to decorate hats and clothes.

clue.text: A long time inside to atone for a bloomer

indicators.note: inside places the long period within the word for atoning

parts.note: to pay for a wrong is to atone for it
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A prisoner serves a lengthy sentence to make amends for a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, but it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A paeony (peony) is a garden plant prized for its large showy blooms.

clue.text: Minute area that was hunted by Maori

parts.note: mo is short for a moment, a minute

explanation.surface: A small patch of land was once a hunting ground for New Zealand's native people.
explanation.definitionFit: The moa was a giant flightless New Zealand bird hunted to extinction by early Maori.

clue.text: Too big? Old hem covers most of fat

indicators.note: covers means the edge word wraps around the shortened fat

parts.note: a verge is an edge or border, a hem

indicators.note: most of means the word for fat loses its last letter

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A dressmaker asks whether a dress is too large, since an old hem hides much of the wearer's bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hem' looks like stitching, but a verge is any border or edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlarge simply means excessively large, too big for the purpose.

clue.text: Non-coms impassioned about Zoroastrian's leader, his god

parts.note: OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not commissioned officers

indicators.note: about means the frenzied word goes around the picked letter

parts.note: mad can mean wildly passionate or frenzied

indicators.note: leader picks out the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Low-ranking soldiers rant about the founder of an ancient Persian faith and his deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Ormazd (Ahura Mazda) is the supreme god of Zoroastrianism; the grid's ORMAND is an OCR slip, as the wordplay needs the Z of Zoroastrian.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormazd is the Zoroastrian supreme deity of light and goodness, the god of Zoroaster's faith.

clue.text: Easily handled in vast, endless, vague domain

indicators.note: in places the nautical word within the shortened vast
endless means the word for vast loses its final letter

parts.note: great means vast
yare is an old nautical word for a ship that answers the helm readily

explanation.surface: Something manageable sits within a huge, unbounded and hazy territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easily handled' is the old sailing word yare, said of a ship that answers the helm readily.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a situation or field that is unclear, not fitting neatly into existing rules.

clue.text: Divinity embraced by Lutherans

indicators.note: embraced by means the letters are held within the word that follows

explanation.surface: A deity is warmly welcomed by Protestant followers of Martin Luther.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was queen of the Greek gods, a goddess and so a divinity.

clue.text: Three stars groomed in Bolton rise

indicators.note: groomed means tidied and rearranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A trio of celebrities is spruced up for an event in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolton is a town near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion's Belt is the line of three bright stars across the middle of the constellation Orion.

clue.text: Hampshire town cook welcomes serenades

indicators.note: welcomes means the cooking word takes the singing phrase inside it

parts.note: to bake is to cook in an oven
to serenade someone is to sing to them

explanation.surface: A chef greets the musicians who perform for diners in a southern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Basingstoke is a large town in Hampshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Basingstoke is a sizable town in the county of Hampshire in southern England.

clue.text: Quite an effort to follow one having the same elevation

indicators.note: to follow means the praise for an effort comes after the numeral

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
'some try!' is a colloquial way of praising quite an effort

explanation.surface: A climber's ascent after another earns praise for reaching an equal height.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometry in geography means equality of height above sea level, so equal elevation.

clue.text: Fit for sailing, shattered in other ways

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boat is ready for the sea, though worn out in various respects.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaworthy vessel is in a fit state to sail safely at sea.

clue.text: Clear stable

definitions.meaning: clear in the sense of certain or in no doubt
stable in the sense of firm and secure

explanation.definitionFit: Sure means both certain (clear in one's mind) and steady or reliable, like a sure foundation.

clue.text: Recalling changes, rejecting the new and reacting badly

indicators.note: changes means the letters are shuffled into a new order
rejecting means a letter is thrown out of the shuffled word

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone recalls revisions, refuses anything novel and responds poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting the new' removes N from RECALLING, and 'changes' rearranges the remaining RECALLIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Being allergic means one's body responds badly to a substance with an immune reaction.

clue.text: Scatty daughter to rear

parts.note: aft means at the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A scatterbrained girl is handed over to be brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft and scatty are both informal words for silly or feather-brained.

clue.text: Not now a person without yearnings?

definitions.meaning: ... happening at present, formerly but not today
read as a whimsical noun phrase, someone who does not long for anything

explanation.definitionFit: No longer means not any more, and split cryptically it suggests 'no longer', someone with no longing.

clue.text: Craters that might be laid out in rings?

definitions.text: Craters that might be laid out in rings?

parts.words: Craters that might be laid out in rings?
parts.note: a crater here is someone who packs goods into crates, and such packers might be prizefighters knocked down in the ring

explanation.definitionFit: Boxers pack things into boxes, as craters pack crates, and boxers are also knocked out in rings.

clue.text: Weed that could give master a licking

definitions.meaning: a wild plant growing where it is not wanted

definitions.text: that could give master a licking
definitions.meaning: a pet's lapping organ could lick its owner, with licking also suggesting a beating

explanation.definitionFit: Dog's-tongue is another name for hound's-tongue, a weedy plant, and a dog's tongue licks its master.

clue.text: Muslim given American backing

indicators.note: backing means the two pieces together are read in reverse

parts.note: if can mean given that, as in 'given the rain'

explanation.surface: A follower of Islam gains support from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support, but it turns IFUS around.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sufi is a Muslim mystic, an adherent of the mystical branch of Islam.

clue.text: Girl cut period before weekend

indicators.note: cut means the final letter of the day is chopped off

parts.note: Friday is the day immediately before the weekend

explanation.surface: A young woman's hours are reduced ahead of Saturday and Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Frida is a girl's name, as in the painter Frida Kahlo.

clue.text: Yard detected missing cases sent back with the rest

indicators.note: sent back means the trimmed letters are then read from right to left
missing cases means each of the two words loses its outer letters, like a book without covers

explanation.surface: Scotland Yard detectives, having failed to find the luggage, returned it along with everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: Trimming the outer letters of Yard and detected leaves ARETECTE, which 'sent back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera is Latin for 'and the rest', used to stand for further similar items.

clue.text: Consciousness of energy and spirit

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for energy in physics
go means vigour or spirit, as in full of go

explanation.surface: Awareness is made up of vitality and liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology the ego is the conscious self, the part of the mind aware of identity.

clue.text: Goal designed to include Bible class hymn

indicators.note: to include means the class abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
designed means arranged to a plan, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, the old school name for Bible study

explanation.surface: A school sets out to add Scripture lessons to its sacred song.
explanation.walkthrough: RI (religious instruction) was the old British school subject of Bible study.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gloria is a hymn of praise sung in Christian worship, from Gloria in excelsis Deo.

clue.text: Hose only kinked between poles

indicators.note: between places the shuffled letters inside the pair of poles

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

indicators.note: kinked means twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden hose is twisted only between its posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' suggests a garden hosepipe, but it means stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings, and hose is a collective word for stockings.

clue.text: Is keeping company about meeting with others of a community?

indicators.note: about means the combined letters are turned round
keeping means the first word holds the company abbreviation inside it

parts.note: taken as written
et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: A question asks whether keeping company and mixing with other people is what makes a community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' is a link word joining the two halves; et al (and others) is the Latin abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Societal means relating to society, the community of people living together.
